# Training and serving capability matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/gates/training-capabilities.py from scripts/gates/training-capabilities.tsv; edit the declaration, not this page. -->

Which architecture can be fine-tuned how, over which checkpoint precision,
and served with adapters and which KV tiers. Every cell names the test that
backs it; a cell with no test is written `-` and means "not offered", never
"untested but probably works". Per-model pages hold the commands. This page
does not record speed or memory figures.

Tests are named `crate/tests/file.rs::test_name` (or `crate/src/file.rs` for a
unit test). A test that needs a real checkpoint or a CUDA card is marked
`(real)` or `(cuda)`; the others run on the CPU backend with random weights.
`gpt2` trains from scratch (see its page) and offers no adapter.

| `glmdsa` | fp32 weights; AdamW state on the device in f32, bf16 or int8 blocks, or in host memory in any format with exact resume (the run's precision, through the generic optimizer-state path); routed experts hold their routed rows only; activations=recompute keeps one layer's activations and replays each layer before its backward, activations=bf16|fp8 also holds the residuals narrow: `glmdsa/tests/it/convergence.rs::glm_overfits_fixed_batch`, `glmdsa/tests/it/optimizer_state.rs::glm_trains_with_narrow_optimizer_state`, `glmdsa/tests/it/optimizer_state.rs::glm_resumes_exactly_with_host_moments`, `glmdsa/tests/it/recompute.rs::glm_recomputes_every_layer_and_narrows_its_boundaries` | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `gpt2` | - | - | - | - | - | - | trains from scratch over a char/BPE corpus through the shared `model::train::fit` loop (no checkpoint to fine-tune, no adapters); activations=recompute keeps one layer's activations and replays each layer before its backward, activations=bf16|fp8 also holds the residuals narrow; weights=f32,window=N streams the layers through a device window with their values and optimizer state on the host, exact resume: `gpt2/tests/it/convergence.rs::engine_memorizes_cyclic_sequence`, `gpt2/tests/it/convergence.rs::engine_learns_copy_through_mask`, `gpt2/tests/it/convergence.rs::loss_improves_with_model_size`, `gpt2/tests/it/recompute.rs::gpt2_recomputes_every_layer_and_narrows_its_boundaries`, `gpt2/tests/it/layer_streamed.rs::gpt2_streams_its_layers_through_a_one_layer_window_and_resumes_exactly` |

No architecture offers a full fine-tune over a quantized or fp8 base. Trainable
parameters, gradients and optimizer moments are held below fp32 only where a
cell says so.

## Checkpoint precision on load

| Source | What stays packed | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Q8_0 GGUF into int8 weights | the blocks are repacked, never expanded to fp32 | `flux2/tests/it/gguf_direct_int8.rs::gguf_int8_is_bit_identical_to_the_fp32_round_trip`, `model/src/int8.rs` |
| brain packed-int8 safetensors | words copied as stored | `checkpoint/src/weightio.rs::with_tensor_u32_chunks_is_memory_bounded` |
| FP8 HF directory into bf16 or NF4 base | nothing: each tensor is dequantized to fp32 on the host, one tensor at a time, then packed; a one-off bounded conversion into a packed file (convert_to_file) lets every later load preserve the NF4 bytes | `qwen35/tests/it/fp8_source.rs::streaming_the_whole_model_keeps_host_allocation_near_one_tensor`, `qwen35/tests/it/convert_base.rs::a_base_converted_once_equals_the_base_converted_on_every_load` |
| Other GGUF quant types (Q4_K and the rest) | nothing: decoded to fp32 and requantized to the requested tier; the packed relayout is tested but no loader uses it | `gguf/tests/it/kquant.rs` |
| Mixed per-tensor formats in one packed file | attention FP8, MLP NF4, embeddings bf16 and norms f32 in one file: every tensor reaches the device in its stored format (no fp32 expansion), the precision report lists each tensor's format and bytes, a fused group of differently stored parts converts per part under an explicit tier or loads as separate weights | `qwen35/tests/it/mixed_precision.rs::every_tensor_reaches_the_device_in_its_stored_format`, `qwen3/tests/it/mixed_precision.rs::every_tensor_reaches_the_device_in_its_stored_format`, `model/tests/it/upload_from_source.rs::a_fused_group_of_mixed_encodings_is_converted_per_part_or_split`, `checkpoint/src/packed/source.rs::a_fused_group_of_mixed_encodings_is_split_or_explicitly_converted` |

A LoRA adapter trains over an FP8 base on qwen3, qwen35 and ricursive. NVFP4
and MX checkpoints have `Weight` storage and execution, and only ricursive's
LoRA trainer offers the NVFP4 release as a base (its "Other" cell). The contributor roadmap for these gaps is
`.agents/roadmap/quantized-training.md`.
